title: Cicero: Essays, Letters, And Orations
description: Reading and study of selected works of Cicero, normally one of the major speeches. Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, and rhetorical points.

title: Prose Of The Empire
description: Reading, translation, and discussion of authors such as Seneca, Pliny, and Tacitus.

title: Roman Epistles
description: Reading, translation, and discussion of the letters of Cicero, Seneca, and Pliny.

title: Sallust
description: Study of one of the extant works of Rome's first great historian: the Bellum Catilinae or the Bellum Iugurthinum. Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, literary, and historical points.

title: Livy
description: Reading and study of the annalistic history of Livy with attention to the author's style, literary, and historical context, and the recent scholarly approaches to the text.

title: Tacitus
description: Study of portions of one of Tacitus' major histories of the early empire (Annales, Historiae), or of the shorter works (Agricola, Dialogus, Germania). Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, literary, and historical points.

title: Caesar
description: Study of Caesar as historian and Latin prose stylist. Extensive reading.

title: Roman Biography
description: Exploration of Roman biographical writing: its historical and literary context, themes, and techniques. Translation and discussion of selections from the biographies of Nepos, Suetonius, and Tacitus, as well as biographical passages from the histories of Sallust, Livy, and Tacitus.

title: Lucretius
description: Reading, translation, and discussion of style, meter and philosophy in Lucretius' epic poem De Rerum Natura.

title: Vergil
description: Reading, translation, and discussion of Vergil's epic poem Aeneid, as well as his Georgics and Eclogues.

title: Ovid
description: Translation and discussion of Ovid's epic or elegiac poetry (Metamorphoses, Fasti, Ars Amatoria, Tristia, Heroides) in its literary, social and historical contexts.

title: Catullus
description: Translation and discussion of Catullus' poetry in its literary, social, and historical contexts.

title: Horace
description: Reading, translation, and discussion of selected poems of Horace (Odes, Epodes, Satires, Epistles) in their literary, social, and historical contexts.

title: Seneca: Tragedies
description: Reading, translation, and discussion of several tragedies by Seneca.

title: Independent Studies In Latin.
description: Independent investigations in Latin language and literature.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor and department chair. upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Latin.

title: Introduction to Latin Prose
description: Reading and analysis of various Latin prose authors to develop reading skills and introduce study of the style and thought of historical, rhetorical and/or philosophical writers.
prerequisites_raw: One year of Latin or more.

title: Latin Prose Composition
description: Study of Latin grammar and syntax through English composition, combined with analysis of Latin prose style in a variety of authors, including Cato, Caesar, Cicero, Sallust, and Tacitus.

title: Roman Epic
description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of authors such as Vergil and Lucan.

title: Roman Elegy
description: Advanced study and discussion of the elegiac works of Tibullus, Propertius, and/or Ovid. Consideration of the genre of elegy in its literary and historical contexts, with special attention to elegiac themes and motifs.

title: Roman Satire
description: Advanced readings in Horace, Juvenal, Persius, and/or Martial.

title: Roman Comedy
description: Advanced study of Plautus and Terence. Reading of complete plays and study of the origins of Roman comedy.

title: The Roman Novel
description: Advanced study of Petronius and/or Apuleius, with attention to the language and style of their satiric novels, and to their social and historical context.

title: Cicero: Essays, Letters, and Orations
description: Advanced reading and study of selected works of Cicero, normally one of the major speeches. Translation; discussion of philological, stylistic, and rhetorical points; introduction to current scholarship.

title: Prose of the Empire
description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of authors such as Seneca, Pliny, and Tacitus.

title: Roman Epistles
description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of authors such as Cicero, Seneca, and Pliny.

title: Sallust
description: Advanced study of one of the extant works of Rome's first great historian: The Bellum Catilinae or the Bellum Iugurthinum. Translations; discussion of philological, stylistic, literary, and historical points; introduction to current scholarship.
